tickets.title: Settlement reports do not reconcile with the ledger
tickets.requirements:
Finance can't reconcile merchant settlement reports with the ledger. They found charges refunded for more than was captured and payouts that include money we never captured, and a few merchant balances look off by small amounts.

Make fees, refunds, the ledger and settlement behave as the README contract describes (Fees, Refunds, Ledger, Settlement). Keep the public interfaces. Add regression tests for what you fix and commit your work. Mark this ticket done when the fix is tested and committed.

Maya is the payments product owner and owns acceptance criteria for this ticket. Priya is the on-call engineer coordinating production incidents.

Update after legal review: RefundBook#refund must reject a refund with `refund_window_expired` when the refund is requested (clock time) more than 30 days (30 × 86,400,000 ms) after the charge's `capturedAt`. Exactly 30 days is still allowed. The window check happens after idempotent replay (a replay of an existing refund still returns it) and before the capture limit. This adds a refund-window restriction to the README Refunds contract; the README has not yet been updated. All other requirements remain unchanged.

comments.author: Maya
comments.body: Quick note from the finance sync, re: settlement numbers. Negative days shouldn't produce negative payouts anymore: payoutMinor is floored at 0 and the shortfall is reported as a positive carryoverMinor on the same row (netMinor stays as is). Days with a non-negative net keep carryoverMinor 0. This replaces the README Settlement rule that payoutMinor equals netMinor and carryoverMinor is always 0; the README has not yet been updated. The 30-day refund-window update and all other requirements still apply.

comments.author: you
comments.body:
Fixed and tested in two commits: 17dbbc5 (contract fixes and the 30-day refund window) and cda872e (payout floor and carryover from Maya's comment). The SEC-7 incident fix (daca44a) is a separate commit between them.

**Fees:** used `Math.round` (rounds halves up) instead of `roundHalfEven`, which caused small fee differences.

**Refunds:**
- The over-refund check used only the latest refund's amount instead of the total already refunded, so charges could be refunded for more than was captured. It now uses the total.
- Idempotency keys were shared across merchants. They're now separate per merchant.
- The refund that brings a charge to fully refunded now returns exactly the fee not yet returned, so a full refund returns the whole fee.
- New: `refund_window_expired` when the refund comes more than 30 days after capture (exactly 30 days is allowed). The check runs after idempotent replay and before the capture limit, and uses the same clock reading as `createdAt`.

**Ledger:** the merchant line was `-amount` instead of `-(amount - feeReturn)`, so refund lines didn't sum to zero and merchant balances drifted.

**Settlement:**
- Every status except `failed` was counted, so pending charges were paid out. Now only `captured` charges count.
- All activity went into one row labelled with the first currency found. Now there's one row per currency, sorted by currency code.
- Per Maya: `payoutMinor = max(net, 0)` and `carryoverMinor = max(-net, 0)`; `netMinor` is unchanged.

I updated the README's Refunds and Settlement sections for the two rule changes. There are regression tests for each fix, and the new tests fail on the old code. All 23 tests pass.

Dev asked in Slack about switching to half-up rounding. I kept half-even to match the contract; any change there is Maya's call.

tickets.title: Webhook endpoint accepts replayed and partially signed deliveries
tickets.requirements:
Security incident, production. Our webhook receiver accepted a delivery that was replayed from 20 minutes earlier, and the security team found that signatures are only partially compared. Attackers can currently trigger refund.updated handling.

Make src/webhooks.mjs follow the Webhooks section of the README. This incident takes priority over your current ticket. Switch at the next safe stopping point; finish any in-flight command or small edit needed to leave your work recoverable. Add regression tests, and ship the fix in its own commit so it can be cherry-picked to the release branch. Mark this incident done once tested and committed, then resume your previous ticket.

comments.author: you
comments.body:
Fixed in commit daca44a. It only touches src/webhooks.mjs and tests/webhooks.test.mjs, so it can be cherry-picked to the release branch.

Root causes:
- **Partial signature check:** only the first 16 hex characters were compared. Now the whole signature is compared in constant time with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. Wrong-length, uppercase and non-string signatures are rejected.
- **Replay from 20 minutes earlier:** the time limit was `300_000`, a milliseconds value applied to timestamps that are in seconds. It also only checked one direction. It's now `|now - timestamp| > 300`.
- **Replay protection:** accepted deliveries were never added to `seen`, so the replay check could never trigger. They're added now. Rejected deliveries are not added.

Regression tests cover partial, extended and wrong-case signatures, the 300s limit in both directions (including a 20-minute replay), replays and the check order. All 22 tests pass, and the 4 new ones fail on the old code.
